title: Find the row with maximum number of 1's
problemStatement: In a binary matrix where each row is sorted (0s then 1s), find the row with the most 1s.
intuition: Per row, the count of 1s is m - index_of_first_1, and that index is a lower bound query.

approaches.title: Brute: count every cell
Optimal: binary search per row
approaches.idea: Lower bound of 1 in each sorted row.
approaches.dryRun:
rows -> first 1 at index 2, 1, none
counts 1, 2, 0 -> row 1

approaches.title: Staircase alternative
approaches.idea: Start top-right and walk left on 1s, down on 0s — O(n + m) total.

commonMistakes: Assuming rows are sorted when they are not
Returning the count instead of the row index
patternRecognition: Sorted rows -> per-row binary search, or a single staircase walk
followUps: Row with most 1s when rows are unsorted
Search in a row/column sorted matrix (#108)
interviewInsight: Offering the O(n + m) staircase walk as a bonus usually lands better than the binary search itself.

related.title: Search in a row and column wise sorted matrix
